lines.text: So in the usual flow (meeting with defects, a failing `follow_up`, more rework, a passing `follow_up`) rework is `closedAt - meetingEnd` and follow-up is `0`, a real value: every follow-up attempt happens inside one tool call. Follow-up time is above zero only when the meeting logged no defects, so the inspection waits in FollowUp from `meetingEnd` until the first `follow_up`. `reworkStart` and `followupStart` stay in `inspection.json` as informational first-occurrence stamps (FM-R1.5).

Property P8 (review v2 issue 4) checks the walk over attempts generated in time order: rework plus follow-up always equals `closedAt - meetingEnd` for a Closed inspection and `abandonedAt - meetingEnd` for an abandoned one.

APIs used, as shown in the SDK v1.x docs ([server.md](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/v1.x/docs/server.md)) and confirmed in the installed type declarations (`dist/esm/server/mcp.d.ts`, `dist/esm/server/stdio.d.ts`, `dist/esm/client/index.d.ts`, `dist/esm/client/stdio.d.ts`):

- `hook gate` reads the command from `tool_input.command`, then `tool_input.cmd` (string values only), until experiment E2 confirms the real field. It uses the payload's `cwd` when it is a non-empty string, else the process working directory. Outside a git repository, or with no `.fagan/inspections/`, a commit is allowed. On a block it prints the inspection IDs and blocking defect IDs, as `insp-0001: D001, D003`, to both stdout and stderr.
- `hook suggest` prints at most one line and swallows every error (message on stderr), so it always exits 0.

- `hook suggest` coverage (FM-R15.2, review v1 issue 5): a changed file counts as covered when its current working-tree blob hash is one of the hashes recorded for that path in a Closed inspection's passing follow-up attempt (`attempts[].blobs`). This includes the Author's rework, which changes the diff after the inspection was opened. Only uncovered files count toward `suggestThresholdLoc`. A byte-equal `diff.patch` still counts as covered. When the uncovered count is above `sizeLimitLoc`, the message says `open_inspection` would refuse it with `SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and asks for the change to be split.

- `hook gate` target repos (FM-R16.2, review v1 issue 6): `gitCommitTargets` in `src/core/gate.ts` returns, for each commit segment, its directory options in the order they apply (`env -C`/`--chdir`, `sudo -D`/`--chdir`, then each `git -C`). The CLI resolves them one after another from the payload `cwd` with `path.resolve`, so a relative `-C` is relative to the previous directory as git documents, and checks the store of every distinct target repo. When blocks come from more than one repo, each is labelled with its root.

- `hook suggest` coverage (FM-R15.2, review v1 issue 5, review v2 issue 2): a changed file counts as covered when its current working-tree blob hash is one of the hashes recorded for that path in a Closed inspection's passing follow-up attempt (`attempts[].blobs`) and its `HEAD` blob equals that inspection's `blobBefore` for it, so both diffs start from the same base. This includes the Author's rework, which changes the diff after the inspection was opened. A covered file still adds its rework drift (`reworkDriftLoc` in `src/core/packet.ts`): the added and deleted lines, compared as multisets of text plus the no-newline flag, that are in only one of the file's diff in `diff.patch` and its current diff. A one-line fix adds 2, new lines add one each, and code added during Rework or while a no-defect inspection waits in FollowUp counts toward `suggestThresholdLoc`. When several Closed inspections cover a file, the smallest drift counts. Uncovered files add all their changed lines. Two trade-offs are accepted: a line moved within the file adds 0, and a file edited again after its inspection closed is uncovered, so all its changed lines count. A byte-equal `diff.patch` still counts as covered. When the count is above `sizeLimitLoc`, the message says `open_inspection` would refuse it with `SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and asks for the change to be split.

- `hook gate` target repos (FM-R16.2, review v1 issue 6, review v2 issue 1): `gitCommitTargets` in `src/core/gate.ts` returns, for each commit segment, its directory options in the order they apply (`env -C`/`--chdir`, `sudo -D`/`--chdir`, then each `git -C`). The tokeniser flags each word: a word is used as written after quote removal; a leading unquoted `~` or `~/` becomes `os.homedir()` unless a character before the first unquoted `/` is quoted (POSIX tilde-prefix rule); a word with a `$` or backtick outside single quotes, another tilde form (`~user`, `~+`), or `*`, `?`, `[`, `{` outside quotes is reported as `null`, because the shell would expand it and the matcher does not. `commitRoot` in `src/cli.ts` resolves the values one after another from the payload `cwd` with `path.resolve`, so a relative `-C` is relative to the previous directory as git documents. After a `null`, later relative values stay unknown and an absolute one is known again. When the directory stays unknown, or the resolved directory is not inside a git repository (including one that does not exist), the commit is checked against the payload `cwd` repo instead. Before this rule, `git -C "$PWD" commit` resolved to `<cwd>/$PWD`, found no repo and was allowed silently. The CLI checks the store of every distinct target repo. When blocks come from more than one repo, each is labelled with its root.

- `follow-up` and `export` run the same service functions as the `follow_up` and `export_report` tools. The CLI acts for the human, who is the Author: `follow-up` passes the role check as `author`, and both commands record their events as `cli:follow-up` / `cli:export` with role `human`. `abandon` records `cli:abandon` with role `human`.
- Failed commands other than the hooks print `{ "code", "message" }` to stderr and exit 1; usage errors print the usage text and exit 1.

lines.text: - Commands inside `sh -c '...'`, `bash -c`, `eval`, scripts, Makefiles, npm scripts and git aliases (the matcher sees only the outer command line).

When the payload `cwd` repo has no open major, a commit into another repo written this way passes.

- `git --git-dir=

` or `--work-tree=

**User story:** As a hook author, I want a CLI over the same core and store, so that hooks (which cannot call MCP tools) can run the ritual's checks.
1. **FM-R15.1** WHEN `fagan serve` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL start the MCP server on stdio and write logs only to stderr.

2. **FM-R15.2** WHEN `fagan hook suggest` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL read the hook payload from STDIN, use its `cwd` (or the process working directory), count changed LOC of the working tree against `HEAD` including untracked files with the same rules as FM-R4.4, and print one short suggestion to run the moderator only if the count exceeds `suggestThresholdLoc`, no inspection is in a non-terminal phase, and no Closed inspection's `diff.patch` equals the current diff. A changed file whose current blob hash equals its blob hash in a Closed inspection's passing follow-up attempt is covered and SHALL not be counted. WHEN the uncovered count also exceeds `sizeLimitLoc` THE SYSTEM SHALL say in the suggestion that `open_inspection` would refuse it with `SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and that the change should be split.

A changed file whose current blob hash equals its blob hash in a Closed inspection's passing follow-up attempt, and whose base blob equals that inspection's `blobBefore` for it, is covered: THE SYSTEM SHALL count for it only its rework drift, the added and deleted lines that differ (compared as multisets) between the file's diff in that inspection's `diff.patch` and its current diff, instead of all its changed lines. So code added during Rework, or while an inspection waits in FollowUp, counts toward `suggestThresholdLoc`. WHEN the count also exceeds `sizeLimitLoc` THE SYSTEM SHALL say in the suggestion that `open_inspection` would refuse it with `SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and that the change should be split.
3. **FM-R15.3** WHEN `fagan hook suggest` finishes, for any input or error THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 0.

4. **FM-R15.4** WHEN `fagan follow-up --latest` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL run follow-up (as FM-R9) on the highest-numbered inspection in Rework or FollowUp, print the result, and exit 0; WHEN no such inspection exists THE SYSTEM SHALL print that and exit 0. `fagan follow-up <id>` does the same for one inspection.

5. **FM-R15.5** WHEN `fagan abandon <id> --reason <text>` runs on a non-terminal inspection with a valid waiver reason THE SYSTEM SHALL move it to Abandoned, set `abandonedAt` and `abandonReason`, and append an event; otherwise it SHALL print the error and exit 1.
**User story:** As the Author, I want agents blocked from committing while an inspection has open majors, so that unresolved majors cannot slip into history.

2. **FM-R16.2** WHEN the command contains a segment (split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&`, parentheses and newlines, plus the bodies of `$(...)` and backticks) whose program is `git` and whose subcommand, after skipping leading environment assignments, the wrappers `command`, `exec`, `time`, `nohup`, `env`, `nice`, `timeout`, `stdbuf`, `xargs`, `sudo` and `doas` with their options, and git global options such as `-c key=value`, `-C <path>` and `--no-pager`, is `commit` THE SYSTEM SHALL treat it as a git commit, and SHALL check the repository it runs in: the payload `cwd` moved, in order, by `env -C`/`--chdir`, `sudo -D`/`--chdir` and each `git -C <path>` (relative paths resolve against the previous directory). lines.text: - E2 and the commit gate (review v1 issue 4): `fagan hook gate` reads `tool_input.command`, then `tool_input.cmd`, and allows the call with a stderr warning when neither is a string (FM-R16.5). If Kiro uses another field, every commit passes. Step 3 acceptance for the gate is "the gate blocked a real `git commit` in a live Kiro session", not only "payload field recorded". Tracked as task 16 in `.kiro/specs/fagan-mcp/tasks.md`.
A second review on 2026-11-16, of the v1 fix pass (commit 647a96b), returned NEEDS_CHANGES with 4 issues. What changed for each, and the tests that cover it (all in `packages/fagan-mcp/test/`):

1. The v1 issue 6 fix opened the gate for `-C` words the shell expands (blocking regression). `git -C "$PWD" commit`, `git -C ~/<repo> commit`, `git -C "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/src" commit` and `env -C $PWD git commit` resolved to folders that do not exist, found no repo and exited 0 while a major was open. The tokeniser in `src/core/gate.ts` now flags each word: `~` and `~/` (unquoted, no quoted character before the first `/`) become the home directory, and a word with `$`, a backtick, another tilde form or an unquoted `*`, `?`, `[` or `{` is reported as unknown. `commitRoot` in `src/cli.ts` checks the payload `cwd` repo when a directory is unknown or is not inside a git repo; an absolute `-C` after an unknown word is known again (FM-R16.2, design.md "Commit gate scope" lists the remaining gap). After the fix, a throwaway script drove a temp repo to Rework with one open major and piped each command into the built `fagan hook gate`: `git commit -m x` and all four commands above exited 2, as did `git -C does-not-exist commit -m x`; `git status` exited 0. Tests: `cli.test.ts` (`FM-R16.2 FM-R16.3 falls back to the payload cwd for -C words the shell would expand or that are not a repo (review v2 issue 1)`, nine commands plus the clean-repo and absolute-path cases) and `gate.test.ts` (`FM-R16.2 reports null for directory words the shell would expand`, `FM-R16.2 resolves quoted, escaped and tilde directory words as the shell would`).

2. `hook suggest` treated any amount of code added to an inspected file during Rework as covered. A covered file now adds its rework drift to the count: the added and deleted lines that differ between its diff in `diff.patch` and its current diff (`reworkDriftLoc` in `src/core/packet.ts`, FM-R15.2, design.md "CLI"). Tests: `packet.test.ts` (`FM-R15.2 rework drift counts the changed lines that differ between two diffs of a file`) and `cli.test.ts` (`FM-R15.2 counts code added during rework against the threshold (review v2 issue 2)`: a one-line fix plus 20 new lines gives 22 changed lines against a threshold of 10, and 20 lines added while a no-defect inspection waits in FollowUp give 20). The v1 issue 5 test now uses threshold 2, because its one-line fix is 2 lines of drift.
3. design.md "Commit gate scope" pointed at `tasks.md` task 15 for the step 3 live-block check. It now points at task 16. No code change.

4. No property checked the rework and follow-up totals. New property P8 in `metrics.property.test.ts` (`FM-R10.1 FM-R10.3 rework plus follow-up equals the time from meetingEnd to closedAt or abandonedAt`) generates time-ordered attempts, with and without defects, and checks the sum, non-negative values and which phase is `null`. Changing `at - since` to `at - start` in `reworkAndFollowupMs`, or dropping `entered.FollowUp = true`, makes it fail (counterexamples `[false,0,[1],"closed",0]` and `[true,0,[],"closed",0]`); both edits were reverted.

The review also listed `no_newline_at_eof` in a `get_packet` result over stdio as untested. The full-lifecycle test in `contract.test.ts` now checks that every unit line returned in Preparation carries the field. All values are `false` there, because every fixture file ends in a newline; the `true` case is covered in-process by `packet.test.ts` (`FM-R4.7 keeps the no-newline-at-end-of-file marker in packet units and report.txt`).

items.question: Is every factual or historical claim either cited or marked "needs citation"?
Do commands, file paths and option names match the code as it is now?
Are numbers, results and examples real outputs rather than invented ones?
Are the steps complete and in an order a new reader can follow?
Do links point to the right pages and use descriptive link text?

checklists.title: JSON, YAML and Kiro configuration checklist

items.question: Does every key and value follow the documented format for this file (for Kiro files, the kiro.dev docs page)?
Are paths, globs and command names correct relative to where the tool reads them?
Do permissions and tool lists grant only what the role or step needs?
Are version numbers, schema versions and IDs consistent with the code that reads this file?
Is the file free of secrets, machine-specific absolute paths and ignored-folder rules for .kiro/?
Would this test fail if the behaviour it names were broken or reverted?
Does the test name carry the requirement ID it checks, and does it check that requirement?
Are edge cases covered: empty, zero, equal, reversed and maximum inputs?
Are temp files, folders and processes cleaned up even when the test fails?
Is the test deterministic: fixed clock, no network, no dependence on run order?
Are loop bounds, comparisons and off-by-one cases right for empty, single and full inputs?
Is every possibly undefined or null value checked before use, without non-null assertions that hide a real gap?
Are promises awaited or returned, and are rejected promises handled?
Do exported function signatures, types and error shapes match what callers and the spec expect?
Is input from outside the process (tool arguments, files, environment, stdin) validated before use?
Are child processes started with argument arrays and never through a shell string?
Are numbers safe from division by zero, NaN and Infinity, and are units (ms, LOC) consistent?
Is data written in a stable order and format so the output is deterministic?
Do names and comments describe what the code actually does?

readings.paraphrase: The design adds a description of property P8. It says that time-ordered follow-up attempts are used to check whether rework time plus follow-up time equals the interval from the meeting's end to closure or abandonment.

The CLI design now requires both accepted working-tree content and a matching base blob before a file counts as covered. It counts differences between the inspected and current added and deleted lines as rework drift, using the smallest drift across matching inspections. The gate description now distinguishes literal directory words, home-directory forms and shell-expanded words. It resolves known directories in order and uses the payload repository when the target remains unknown or is outside a repository.

The gate-scope list adds shell-expanded directory arguments as a documented case where the payload repository is checked instead of the expanded destination. It states that this can allow a commit into another repository when the payload repository has no open major. The payload-field experiment reference changes from task 15 to task 16.

The property-test table gains P8, linked to the metrics property test and requirements FM-R10.1 and FM-R10.3. The row describes generated attempts ending in closure or abandonment, a total-duration equality, non-negative durations and null values for phases that were not entered.

The suggestion requirement changes how accepted files contribute to the line threshold. A file now needs matching accepted content and a matching inspection base to count as covered. For such a file the count includes added and deleted lines that differ from the inspected diff, so additions made during Rework or while waiting in FollowUp contribute to a later suggestion.

The commit-gate requirement adds rules for interpreting directory arguments. Literal words are used after quote removal, while an eligible leading tilde becomes the home directory. If unresolved shell syntax leaves the target unknown, or the resulting directory is outside a repository, the gate checks the repository associated with the payload working directory.

The task list adds a completed review-v2 section with four items: gate directory fallback and home-directory expansion, rework drift in suggestion counts, the task-16 reference in the scope documentation, and the property relating rework and follow-up totals to the inspection end time. It also lists the associated requirement IDs.

The experiment document adds a review-v2 account covering directory-word handling, rework-drift counting, a task-number change and the new metrics property. It names the related tests, records the command outcomes reported by the earlier experiment, and describes two temporary property-test mutations. It also distinguishes the newline-marker assertion over stdio from the in-process case where the marker is true.
The CLI imports the operating system's home-directory function. Its path import is expanded to include the absolute-path predicate alongside the existing path-resolution function.
The CLI adds gateRoot to the functions it imports from the service module. The surrounding imports continue to include gateBlocks and the inspection service operations.

The CLI adds a homeDir helper that returns a nonempty home-directory string or null. It also adds commitRoot, which walks directory arguments from the supplied base. A null argument makes the current target unknown; a later absolute argument establishes a new known target. The function then resolves a repository root, using the base repository when the target is unknown or does not identify a repository.

The hook passes the detected home directory into gitCommitTargets. Instead of directly reducing each directory chain into a path, it resolves each chain through commitRoot and collects distinct non-null repository roots. It then asks gateBlocks for each root and retains blocks that have not already been collected for the same inspection and repository.

The gate module's introductory comment adds the directory-word interpretation rules. It describes quote removal, expansion of an eligible leading tilde, and null results for syntax whose shell expansion is not evaluated. It says the CLI uses the payload working directory for those null targets.

The tokenizer introduces a ShellWord object containing text, a literal flag and a tilde flag, plus a set of unquoted expansion characters. shellSegments becomes a text-only projection of the new shellWordSegments function. That function stores and resets the flags for each word and adds a helper that turns off tilde expansion when quoting occurs inside the tilde prefix.

When the tokenizer encounters dollar-parenthesis or backtick command substitution, it now parses the nested command into ShellWord segments rather than string segments. Both branches also mark the containing word as nonliteral while retaining the existing position-advance behavior.
The tokenizer calls quotedChar before reading the contents of a single-quoted string. The surrounding code continues to append the quoted contents to the current word.
The tokenizer calls quotedChar when it enters a double-quoted string. It then continues through the existing loop that reads the string's contents.

Inside the double-quote loop, an unescaped dollar sign now marks the current word as nonliteral before the character is appended. The surrounding branch still advances through the input one character at a time.
When a backslash escapes a character other than a newline, the tokenizer now calls quotedChar before appending that character. It continues to mark the word as present after the append.

The unquoted-character path now marks dollar signs and configured expansion characters as nonliteral. A tilde at the start of a word enables the tilde flag and begins a tilde prefix; an unquoted slash ends that prefix. The character is then appended through the existing word-building path.

A literalWord helper constructs ShellWord objects from strings. gitCommitDirs changes its input and return types from string arrays to ShellWord arrays, and its directory accumulator now stores those objects. The first loop reads each word's text when identifying leading assignments and wrappers.

Wrapper-option parsing now reads option text from ShellWord objects. For a long option with an equals sign, a captured directory value inherits the option's literal flag and has its tilde flag set to false. For a separate directory operand, the parser stores the following ShellWord object itself.

The Git-command portion of gitCommitDirs reads the program and option names from ShellWord text. It compares the text after a double dash with commit, returns the accumulated directories when it encounters the commit subcommand, and stores the following ShellWord as a directory when the option text is exactly -C. Option advancement still depends on whether the option takes a separate value.

isGitCommitSegment now wraps its string inputs as literal ShellWord objects. The new dirWordPath function returns null for nonliteral words, returns ordinary literal text unchanged, and expands supported tilde forms when a home directory is available. gitCommitTargets accepts that home directory, obtains flagged word segments, keeps commit directory chains and maps each directory word to its path or null.

The packet module adds reworkDriftLoc to compare two diffs for one file. Binary or excluded files contribute zero. For other files it builds balances keyed by changed-line kind, newline-at-end flag and text, adding counts from the inspected diff and subtracting counts from the current diff. The result is the sum of the absolute balances.
The service module adds imports for parseUnifiedDiff and the DiffFile type. The surrounding imports remain the clock, error, follow-up and JSON helpers.
The service module adds reworkDriftLoc to its packet-helper import alongside countChangedLoc and buildPacket.

The service module introduces an AcceptedFile interface for content accepted by a closed inspection. It stores the packet file's base blob hash and an optional parsed diff representing what the inspection read.

Suggestion coverage changes from sets of accepted hashes to a nested map containing accepted content, its base hash and its inspected diff. Closed inspection patches are parsed and associated with their passing follow-up blobs. For each current file, the service finds accepted entries with matching content and base, counts the minimum rework drift when matches exist, and otherwise counts all changed lines. The suggestion text now reports the number of covered files and the drift they contribute.

The service extracts repository-root lookup into gateRoot. It returns null when lookup reports that the directory is outside a Git repository and rethrows other errors. gateBlocks calls the helper and returns an empty block list for a null root before continuing with inspection-store processing.
The CLI tests add homedir to their operating-system imports and relative to their path imports. The existing tmpdir and join imports remain.
The CLI tests add the NOTES fixture to the values imported from the shared fixture module.

The CLI tests add cases for directory words containing parameters, substitutions, tildes and literal unresolved paths. The new test creates an inspection with an open major and expects gate exit code 2 for the listed commands. It also describes checks starting from a clean repository and distinguishes an absolute directory after an unknown value from a relative directory after one. An existing missing-directory case gains an explanatory comment.

The suggestion test for a closed inspection changes its configured threshold from zero to two. The added comment relates that threshold to a one-line rewrite, counted as two changed lines of rework drift.

A new CLI test adds twenty exported constants during rework, records the rework and invokes follow-up. It expects a suggestion reporting twenty-two changed lines against a threshold of ten and naming the covered files' drift. A second case adds twenty lines while a no-defect inspection is waiting in FollowUp and expects those twenty lines to appear in the suggestion count after closure.

The stdio contract test now flattens the lines returned in the preparation packet, asserts that at least one line exists, and expects every no_newline_at_eof value to be false. Its comment notes that the fixture files all end in a newline.

The gate matcher tests add two groups of directory-argument examples. The first expects null for words involving shell parameters, substitutions, unquoted expansion characters, unsupported tilde forms or a missing home directory. The second expects literal or home-expanded paths for quoted, escaped and eligible tilde forms, including examples where quoting within the tilde prefix or an equals-sign option leaves the tilde unchanged.

The metrics property test generates whether a meeting had defects, a meeting offset, up to six failure gaps, a terminal outcome and a final time gap. It builds ordered attempts and computes metrics for each case. Across 500 generated runs, its assertions compare combined rework and follow-up time with the elapsed interval, check non-negative values, and match null durations and phase-not-reached reasons to which phases were entered.
The packet tests add the DiffFile type to their diff imports and reworkDriftLoc to their packet-helper imports. The remaining imports shown in the unit are unchanged.

A new packet test constructs small parsed diffs and compares their rework-drift counts. It expects zero for the same diff, two for a rewritten added line, three for three additional lines in either argument order, and two when the final-newline marker changes. It also expects an excluded package-lock file to contribute zero.

defects.description: The directory chain records only a token exactly equal to -C, so Git's attached form -C/path is skipped as an option without recording its target. A git -C/other/repo commit issued from a clean payload repository is checked against that clean repository and can pass while the target repository has an open major.
